_what: Watersound West Bay Center -- the commercial centre at the community entrance, and its tenants.
_why_this_file_exists: Karen asked for the area to be marked as West Bay Center and for its tenants to be
named. It is not part of the community, is not in any recorded plat we hold, and no
county layer carries it yet -- the parcel layer has no legal description or
subdivision mentioning it, and PlanningProjects returns nothing here. So it is drawn
from Karen's own knowledge of the ground, and labelled as approximate.
_how_measured: Karen drew the area as a red box directly on our own rendered poster and sent it
back. That is the easiest annotation this project has ever had to recover, because
the projection is ours: her screenshot registers to the poster, and the poster
The registration is on the LANDMARK PINS, not on image correlation. Correlating the
whole frame only reached 8.9 sigma -- the sheet is mostly flat sand and watermark,
so a correlator has little to bite on -- and left roughly 200 m of slop. The coral
pins are small, distinctive, identical in both images, and we know exactly where we
drew them. All 9 matched, and a least-squares fit on the matched pairs closed to
rms 2.8 poster px, which is 2.8 m on the ground.
Her box was then reduced to its minimum-area rectangle, since she drew it tilted to
follow the map's own 40 degree rotation.
Chain: her px -> poster px -> figure fraction -> axes fraction -> rotated Mercator
_accuracy: The RECOVERY is good to about 3 m. The BOX ITSELF is a freehand sketch and is not,
and does not claim to be, a parcel boundary. As drawn it covers about 191 acres,
which is larger than the ~110 acres trade press gives the centre, so treat it as
'the centre is in here' and nothing finer. It is styled to read as approximate:
dashed edge, no hard corners implied, and no acreage printed on the map.
_clipped_at_hwy79: Karen's box runs across Highway 79. The centre does not: her own Google aerial and
her drone photo both show it entirely WEST of the highway, with 79 on the right of
frame in each. So the block is clipped to the west side of Hwy 79 using the county's
own highway centreline. That is applying a known real constraint rather than
inventing a boundary -- the alternative was to publish a commercial centre sitting
on top of a state road.
_tenants_source: Karen, who has been on the site. Publix she confirmed separately and has photographed
under construction; St. Joe's own site confirms the centre at ~350,000 sq ft of
leasable space at build out (use that figure, not the 500,000 in trade press).
Names are hers. Google's listing for the cart dealer reads 'Electric Cart Watersound'.
